findings.title: The commits at Task 4 and Task 6 leave the MCP package failing typecheck
findings.description:
Task 3 narrows `GuideMethod` to `'submodule' | 'clone' | 'tarball'`. `guideTools.ts` still has `z.enum(['submodule', 'clone', 'manual'])` at line 101 and passes that value to `manager.install(strategy, source)` at line 116. That is a type error in `@context-forge/mcp-server` until Task 7. Task 5 also changes what `resolveStrategy()`/`install()` return, which can break CLI callers. Yet Task 4 commits `refactor(core): rename…` and Task 6 commits `fix(core): …` after running only the core suite. That breaks the rule that commits sit at working, tested points.
**Fix:** pick one:
- Merge the commits at Task 4 and Task 6 into one commit after Task 8, with a monorepo-wide typecheck and test run as its success criterion.
- Move the minimal `guideTools.ts` enum and narrowing change into Task 3, and have the Task 4 and Task 6 success criteria run `pnpm -r typecheck`.

findings.title: Task 17 appends `GUIDE_OFFLINE_REMEDIATION` a second time
findings.description:
`withNetworkErrorHint()` already appends `GUIDE_OFFLINE_REMEDIATION` when an error message matches a network pattern (line 48). Task 13 routes the timeout through that function, and Task 14 asserts that the `gitExec` rejection already contains `GUIDE_OFFLINE_REMEDIATION`. Task 17 then tells the implementer to "rethrow with `GUIDE_OFFLINE_REMEDIATION` appended (mirror `setup-ide.ts:113`)". So for timeouts and network failures, the user would see the remediation text twice. Task 18 only asserts that the text is present, so the duplicate would pass the tests. (`setup-ide.ts:114` is a different case: there it adds context to its own message, not to a `gitExec` error.)
**Fix:** state which layer owns the remediation text. Either Task 17 appends it only when the message doesn't already contain it, or it relies on `gitExec` and appends nothing. Add a Task 18 assertion that the text appears exactly once.

findings.title: Task 15 contradicts itself about where the timeout is set
findings.description:
The first bullet gives the signature `init(operationPath: string)` and says it always runs with `{ timeoutMs: GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS }`. The second bullet says `sync()` calls `init()` "without the timeout: pass the timeout as an `init()` option". Those can't both be true: if `init()` always applies the timeout, `sync()` becomes time-bounded, which breaks D10. If the timeout is an option, the signature is wrong and `ensureCheckout()` (Task 17) has to pass it. A junior implementer can't tell which one is intended.
**Fix:** state one signature, e.g. `init(operationPath, opts?: { timeoutMs?: number })`. Say that `ensureCheckout()` passes `GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS` and `sync()` passes nothing. Add a Task 16 or Task 18 check that the auto-init path passes the timeout.

findings.title: The CLI warning for `manual` in the config file is never tested
findings.description:
One success criterion reads: "A project whose shared config has `guide.git_strategy: manual` installs as tarball with the same warning." Task 6(b) only checks that core *reports* the alias. Task 7 adds the CLI code that prints the warning for the config case. Task 8 tests only the `--strategy manual` flag. Nothing checks that the config-file case actually prints a warning to stderr.
**Fix:** add a case to Task 8 where the shared config sets `guide.git_strategy: manual` and `cf guides install` is run with no flag. Assert that the install uses tarball and that the deprecation line appears on stderr only.

findings.title: The alias warning is printed in two command files
findings.description: Task 7 prints the deprecation warning in the `guides install` action. Task 26 repeats the same normalize-then-warn step in `init.ts`. That is two copies of the same wording. Have Task 7 export one small helper, e.g. `normalizeStrategyFlag(raw)`, and have Task 26 call it.

findings.title: It's unclear where `operationPath` gets resolved
findings.description: Task 17 says `ensureCheckout()` resolves `operationPath` the same way `getGuideContext()` does. Task 19 passes `operationPath` into `ensureGuideReady()`. Task 22 (MCP) doesn't say how the MCP tools get it. Pick one owner: either the caller resolves it and passes it in, or `ensureCheckout()` resolves it internally. Then say so in Tasks 17, 19 and 22.

findings.title: Task 27's `.gitmodules` check is meaningless if `guidesInstallAction` is mocked
findings.description: Task 27 asserts both that `guidesInstallAction` is called with `tarball` and that no `.gitmodules` file is created. If the test mocks `guidesInstallAction`, the second check passes no matter what. Either assert only the arguments passed through, or run a real tarball install into a temp directory. The walkthrough in Task 32 covers the real end-to-end case either way.

findings.title: Commit markers are inline text, not plain `**Commit**:` lines, and Task 32 mentions a merge
findings.description: The commit points are written as "Commit: `…`" inside checkbox items. The convention is a plain `**Commit**:` line, never a checkbox. The commit points themselves are in sensible places, apart from the problem with Task 4 and Task 6 above. Task 32's "PM reviews before merge to `main`" is a merge/approval step, which the project rules say not to put in a task file. Drop it.

findings.title: Success criteria coverage
findings.description:
Each criterion maps to tasks:
- **Auto-init on `cf build`, plus `--json`:** Tasks 17–21.
- **`cf guides info` shows `Checkout: not initialized`:** Tasks 10 and 24.
- **Warning when the checkout is out of sync:** Tasks 17, 18 and 21.
- **`--strategy manual` installs as tarball:** Tasks 7 and 8.
- **`cf init --strategy`:** Tasks 26 and 27.
- **Help text:** Tasks 25 and 27.
- **Managed-directory line and README:** Tasks 28–30.
- **A malformed config fails the install:** Task 6(c).
- **The grep checks and the no-silent-catch rule:** Tasks 3, 5 and 32.
- **CHANGELOG and DEVLOG:** Task 31.

No task falls outside the slice's scope.

findings.title: Sequencing and proportionality
findings.description: Dependencies run in one direction: rename → detection and init → `ensureCheckout` → call sites → `cf init` and help → notice and docs. None are circular. The Task 9 fixture is built before every test that uses it. Thirty-two tasks with effort 1–3 each is reasonable for a slice covering three issues. Tasks 10 and 11 could be merged, but that's optional. The slice states no NFRs, so no load test is needed.
